research_question: In pregnant women, does antenatal supplementation with any iron-containing supplement (iron alone, iron+folic acid, or multiple micronutrients with iron), compared with the same supplement without iron or with placebo/no treatment, reduce the risk of maternal iron-deficiency anaemia at term (haemoglobin <110 g/L plus at least one additional laboratory indicator of iron deficiency, measured at >=37 weeks' gestation)?
treatment_label: Iron-containing supplement during pregnancy (oral or parenteral iron, alone or combined with folic acid/multiple micronutrients)
control_label: Same supplement without iron, placebo, or no treatment
outcome_description: Maternal iron-deficiency anaemia at term: number/proportion of women with haemoglobin below 110 g/L together with at least one additional laboratory indicator of iron deficiency (e.g. low serum ferritin, low transferrin saturation, raised soluble transferrin receptor, low mean cell volume), assessed at 37 weeks' gestation or later. Trials reporting zero events in both arms are treated as not estimable and excluded from pooling.
positive_direction: A positive effect (risk ratio below 1 / positive signed effect size) means the iron-containing supplement reduced the risk of maternal iron-deficiency anaemia at term relative to the no-iron/placebo control.
search_queries: iron supplementation pregnancy randomized controlled trial anaemia
antenatal iron folic acid supplement maternal haemoglobin trial outcome
iron deficiency anaemia pregnant women supplementation placebo controlled effect
inclusion_criteria: Studies of pregnant women receiving an iron-containing supplement (any dose, route, or regimen; alone or with other micronutrients)
Includes a comparison group receiving the same supplement without iron, a placebo, or no treatment
Reports any quantitative maternal haematological or iron-status outcome (e.g. anaemia or iron-deficiency anaemia event counts, haemoglobin, ferritin) from which an effect size can be derived
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, narrative review, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)
No comparison between an iron-containing treatment condition and a no-iron/placebo/no-treatment control condition
No quantitative outcome data usable for an effect size (no event counts/proportions, means with SDs, t/F statistics, or risk/odds ratios reported)
Completely unrelated to iron supplementation in pregnancy (e.g. non-pregnant populations, non-iron interventions, animal studies)
moderators_to_extract: Iron dose and dosing frequency (daily vs intermittent)
Co-supplementation (iron alone vs iron+folic acid vs multiple micronutrients)
Baseline anaemia prevalence / country income setting
Gestational age at supplementation start and duration
Risk of bias / randomisation and blinding quality
effect_size_note: Pool as risk ratio (RR) of maternal iron-deficiency anaemia at term using event counts per arm; double-zero-event trials are not estimable and are excluded from pooling. Random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird or REML) model with RR<1 favouring iron supplementation.
